message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 201, "amount_cents": 3873}, {"order_id": 203, "amount_cents": 18687}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly. Next I need the orders so I can see which customers are in the batch and check the refunds against them.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is smaller than its order (201: 3873 of 4135; 203: 18687 of 33625), so nothing looks wrong. I'll get the net balance for the first customer, acme, before recording any payout.
Acme's net_balance of 54385 matches the ledger: orders 200 and 203 total 73072, less refund 203 of 18687. Alpha's refund work checks out for this customer, so I'll record acme's payout.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get the net balance for birch, the second customer in the batch, and check it against the ledger before paying.
Birch's orders are 201 (4135) and 204 (39885), totaling 44020. Less refund 201 (3873) gives 40147, which matches net_balance. Alpha's refund work checks out for birch, so I'll record the payout.

Acme and birch are paid. The last customer in the batch is cobalt, with orders 202 (30107) and 205 (2972) and no refunds, so the expected net is 33079. I'll get cobalt's net balance and check it against that before paying.
Cobalt's net_balance of 33079 matches the ledger: orders 202 (30107) and 205 (2972), with no refunds. All three customers now reconcile, so I'll record cobalt's payout.
All three customers in the batch (acme, birch, cobalt) have been paid. Each net_balance matched the ledger orders minus refunds, and every record_payout returned ok.
